questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests ability to design a runtime-extensible backend with a clean interface, minimal FAB (feature-flag) API, and safe runtime swapping.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy pattern for pluggable backends
- Registry for runtime extension
- Atomic swap and cache coherence trade-offs

## Code Example

```javascript
// Interfaces and usage sketch
interface IFlagBackend { getFlag(name:string, context?:any): boolean; }
class FlagCore { constructor(private backend:IFlagBackend){ } isEnabled(name:string, ctx?:any){ return this.backend.getFlag(name, ctx); } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test swapping backends without downtime?
- How would you implement per-tenant flags and cache invalidation?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a pluggable, runtime-extendable auth system with strong tenant isolation, security, and observability. Demonstrates plugin loading, DI patterns, and security considerations critical at scale.

## Key Concepts

- Plugin architecture with dynamic loading
- Tenant isolation and per-tenant configuration
- Authentication flows: login, refresh, logout
- Security: short‑lived tokens, revocation, audit trails

## Code Example

```typescript
interface LoginRequest { provider: string; tenantId: string; credentials: any }
interface AuthResult { token: string; expiresAt: number }
interface AuthProvider {
  login(req: LoginRequest): Promise<AuthResult>
  refresh(token: string): Promise<AuthResult>
  logout(token: string): Promise<void>
}
interface ProviderFactory {
  create(tenantId: string, config: any): AuthProvider
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you version and hot-swap providers without downtime?
- How would you test provider isolation and revocation at scale?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Gateways must adapt routing logic without redeploys; runtime policies test flexibility and thread-safety.

## Key Concepts

- Strategy and Registry patterns
- Precedence and isolation
- Concurrency-safe dynamic registration

## Code Example

```javascript
interface Policy {
  matches(req: Request): boolean
  routeFor(req: Request): string
}
class PolicyRegistry {
  register(name: string, p: Policy, priority?: number): void
  resolve(req: Request): string | null
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How to handle conflicting matches and policy precedence?
- How would you hot-swap policies in a live gateway without dropping requests?
